our interns are employees.
they do real work, on real projects, side by side with some of the industry's brightest minds.
interns get hands-on with never-before-seen technologies and the latest software and hardware developments.

explore early-talent programs intern ignite mba phd new college grad being an intern is the best way to kick-start your journey at nvidia, as it's our primary pipeline for new college grads and early-in-career hiring.
you'll take part in meaningful work, make a difference on real projects, connect with the greatest minds in our industry, and build lifelong connections.
whether you're pursuing a bs, ms, phd, or mba, we offer year-round internships-for a minimum of 12 weeks-with great benefits.
i've been able to talk with everyone-from executives to other interns-while exploring a variety of disciplines.
having exposure to a breadth of people and projects has been very helpful in developing skills that better my community.
- david, trustworthy ai intern the nvidia ignite program gives you everything you need to start building your career-a whole lot earlier than you might expect.

this inclusive, 12-week summer pre-internship program was created to give current freshmen and sophomores from a wide range of backgrounds a chance to work hands-on with real technical experts on real projects.
it's a fully immersive experience covering the products, culture, and ecosystem that make nvidia a truly unique place to ignite your future.
the ignite program was a true catalyst for me.
the group of people i met became a strong support system, and we've stayed connected ever since.
that sense of community continues to motivate me.
- sergio, ignite intern the nvidia mba program is designed to help interns and new college grads develop into the next generation of corporate leaders.
through our best-in-class programs, we also provide powerful upleveling and organic growth tools to help professionals pivot industries and pursue lifelong learning.
at nvidia, i was given the resources, autonomy, and unwavering support to push my limits and dream bigger than ever.
my team not only challenged me but also lifted me up, helping me unlock potential i never imagined i could reach in just one summer.

- paul, mba intern phds at nvidia have the opportunity to make an impact across the company-not only within our world-class research organization, but also in engineering, product, and other technical teams.
our researchers are advancing technology and publishing at top conferences, while many other teams apply cutting-edge methods to build real products, platforms, and services.
whether you're passionate about pushing scientific discovery or applying research to solve real-world challenges, there's a place for your expertise at nvidia.
i had the opportunity to work on impactful projects closely aligned with my research interests, allowing me to both contribute meaningfully and deepen my technical expertise.
- swapnil, phd intern nvidia empowers everyone to contribute as you get your hands on the latest computing technology.
within our new college graduate (ncg) program, you'll be able to influence areas ranging from high-performance computing and graphics to edge computing, networking, autonomous machines, and more.
we provide great benefits that include espp, tuition reimbursement, continuous learning and development programs, paid time off, and more.

our university students and early-in-career hires will one day become our future leaders-overseeing large teams, bringing innovative products to market, and making a difference by helping us take on the world's greatest challenges.
at nvidia, it's unique how leadership isn't restricted by title or seniority.
i have the autonomy to guide my team toward shared goals.
that's not something that you expect to feel as an intern or new college graduate, and i felt that on day one.

jsip is intended for undergraduate students in their first or second year at the time of applying who are passionate about computer science and have also experienced barriers to opportunity within the field.
jsip represents a unique curriculum for jane street - this program is more rigorous than most.
jsip fellows will learn and develop their programming skills in a collaborative, fast-paced environment to help prepare them for a career in software engineering.
it's called an immersion program for good reason!
application deadline: sunday, february 8th, 2026, at 11:59 p.m.
est.
while first- and second-years are welcome to apply, we will consider second-year applications on a rolling basis, while first-year applications will be reviewed in february.
if you have any questions, please reach out to jsip@janestreet.com.

apply to jsip 2026 who jsip is for undergraduate students in their first or second year at the time of applying who have aspirations in software engineering and have also experienced barriers to access and opportunity within computer science.
more info when our next jsip event will run mid-june to mid-august and will take place in jane street's nyc office.
cost housing, travel to and from the program, meals, and organized social activities will be covered by jane street.
there is no admission fee to attend jsip.
$12500 scholarship jane street will award a $12500 scholarship to each jsip fellow to support future educational opportunities.
for any questions about how this scholarship may affect any financial aid or other financial assistance, please contact your school's financial aid office.
more about jsip during the first few weeks of the program, you'll learn from full-time jane street software engineers and dive deep into computer science fundamentals.
you'll also learn ocaml, jane street's favored programming language, along with the ins and outs of the functional programming that is so crucial to our business.
during the remainder of the program, you'll take the concepts you learned in the first few weeks and apply them to larger, structured projects.
from putting together a design doc, to writing robust and maintainable code, you'll get the chance to plan and execute a complex swe project.
you'll also learn best practices when it comes to applying and interviewing for future swe internships, and gain an in-depth understanding of what a career in software engineering could look like.
diversity of thought and contribution is what allows our firm to stay bold and nimble.
many of us had no previous experience with finance or ocaml when we arrived, and jsip requires no such experience - only a penchant for programming and a curious mind.
faqs who is the program for?

to qualify for this program, you must be a current first- or second- year undergraduate student (matriculated in 2024 or 2025) who intends to complete your college or university's introduction to computer science course(s) by june 2026, and has experienced barriers to access and opportunity within computer science.
our definition of such barriers is broad; they could be related to personal circumstances or financial hardship.
we acknowledge the breadth of challenges that could lead a high-achieving student to be under resourced or under exposed to advanced programming opportunities.

examples include, but are not limited to: being a first-generation college student, experiencing hardship relating to identifying with an underrepresented ethnic/racial minority group, being pell grant eligible, having notable need for financial assistance, attending an under-resourced or rural school, coming from a marginalized community, or experiencing other personal hardship.
this list is not exhaustive, and we encourage any student who is interested and believes they fit the criteria for the program to apply.
participants must be authorized to be employed in the u.s.
without a visa sponsorship now or in the future, regardless of whether the sponsorship would be from an employer or through a school or university.
what is the application process?
to apply to jsip, we ask that you submit a brief application along with your resume.
following your submission, some additional information may be requested and from there, you may be invited to interview.
more details will be provided to applicants as they move forward in the process.
what are the housing arrangements?
jsip fellows will live in a corporate apartment-style building.
each person will have their own fully furnished living space and access to several amenities, including but not limited to a fully equipped kitchen and in-building laundry.
are program dates flexible?
if i have other obligations that might interfere with my time at jsip, can i still attend?

unfortunately the program dates (mid-june to mid-august) are not flexible and if you are accepted into the program, you will be required to confirm that you are available for the full duration of the program.
is there an option to attend jsip online?
at this time, there is no option to attend jsip virtually.

students & grads summits: discover an exciting career capital one's s&g summits are two- to five-day events for undergraduate students to meet with leaders and associates, learn what it's like to work here and prepare for future internship or full-time opportunities.
the summits are: capital one's analyst summit: get insight into what it's like to be a business analyst, a job that helps improve processes and products through strategic consulting.

during this two-day event, you'll gain analytical skills, network with business analysts and participate in a live case interview prep workshop to help you prepare for the analyst early internship program, analyst internship program or analyst development program.
when is the program: may, august who we're looking for: first-year students or sophomores pursuing a quantitative/stem major.

the summit culminates with a hackathon and project demos to capital one leaders.
when is the program: may, august, january who we're looking for: sophomores with beginner coding experience pursuing a computer science/stem major.

for more info and to indicate your interest: tech early experiences - techee@capitalone.com capital one's product summit: this two-day event will give you an inside look of what it means to be a product manager at capital one.

you'll meet with product managers and learn skills to innovate, influence and drive technology solutions-important factors for our analyst early internship program, product development internship program and product development program.

you'll come away with skills that will help you in your application to the management internship program or management development program.
